prompt: Make the jump feel forgiving: add a double jump and a 0.1 s jump buffer.

config.plan_model: Agent-tool model parameter 'sonnet' (Claude Code sub-agent; the harness did not report the resolved model id)
config.how: one fresh general-purpose sub-agent per plan, reads a job file with project brief + the developer prompt, writes numbered plan (<=8 steps, no code) via Write; not Claude Code plan mode

plans.text:
1. Read player.gd and the Player scene to understand the current movement, gravity, jump input handling, and how floor detection is done. Also check the Input Map for the jump action name.
2. Define the tunable values as exported variables on the Player: maximum number of air jumps (set to 1) and buffer duration (0.1 s), so they can be adjusted in the editor without touching logic.
3. Add jump-buffer logic: when the jump button is pressed, record a short countdown timer instead of requiring an immediate grounded state, and decrement it every physics frame.
4. Consume the buffer on landing: if the timer is still active the frame the player touches the floor, trigger the jump automatically and clear the timer so it cannot fire twice.
5. Add double-jump logic: track remaining air jumps, reset the count whenever the player is on the floor, and allow a jump in mid-air while the count is above zero, decrementing it on use.
6. Make the interaction between the two features sensible: a buffered press while airborne should use the double jump only if one is available, and the first jump off the ground must not also spend the air jump.
7. Decide how the second jump looks and sounds (same velocity as the first, optional animation or sprite flip), and check that variable-height jump cutting, if present, still behaves correctly on both jumps.
8. Playtest in level_01.tscn and the enemy interactions: verify early, late, and rapid presses, confirm the air jump resets after landing on TileMapLayer platforms and after stomping an enemy, and tune the values.

1. Read player.gd to learn how movement, gravity, jump input, and floor detection are currently handled, and note any existing jump-related constants or input actions in the project's Input Map.
2. Define the desired behavior up front: one extra mid-air jump, and a 0.1 s window in which a jump press made just before landing is remembered and fires on touchdown. Expose the buffer time and max jumps as tunable exported values.
3. Add a jump counter that resets whenever the player is on the floor, and allow a second jump while airborne that consumes the extra charge. Decide whether the double jump has the same strength as the first or a slightly weaker one.
4. Add a buffer timer that starts when jump is pressed and counts down each physics frame. When the player lands while the timer is still active, trigger the jump automatically and clear the buffer.
5. Make sure the two features interact cleanly: a buffered press on landing should count as the first jump, walking off a ledge should still leave the double jump available, and a single press must never trigger both a jump and a double jump in the same frame.
6. Check the Sprite2D animation logic and any enemy-stomp or bounce code in player.gd so the new air jump plays the right animation and does not conflict with other velocity changes.
7. Playtest in level_01.tscn with the debug view on, testing rapid taps, early presses just before landing, ledge drops, and stomping enemies, then tune the values until it feels forgiving but not floaty.
8. Review the final diff to confirm that only player.gd (and the Input Map, if needed) changed, and that the scene tree and other scenes were left untouched.

1. Read player.gd to understand the current movement, gravity, jump, and floor-detection logic, and note the existing input action names and tuning variables.
2. Check the Input Map in project settings for the jump action so the buffer and double jump reuse it rather than adding a new one.
3. Add exported tuning variables for the jump buffer duration (0.1 s), the maximum number of air jumps (1), and the double-jump strength, so they can be tweaked in the inspector.
4. Implement the jump buffer by recording the time of each jump press and, while that record is still within 0.1 s, firing the jump as soon as the player is grounded.
5. Implement the double jump with an air-jump counter that is reset on landing and decremented when a jump is made in mid-air, giving a slightly different upward velocity from the ground jump.
6. Make sure the two features interact cleanly: a buffered press consumed on landing must not also spend the air jump, and walking off a ledge should still leave the air jump available.
7. Playtest in level_01.tscn, checking early, late, and rapid-repeat jump presses, jumps next to the TileMapLayer edges, and contact with both enemy types, then adjust the tuning values.
8. Add feedback for the double jump, such as a distinct animation frame or sound, only if the Player scene already has a suitable hook, and keep the change limited to player.gd and its inspector values.

1. Read player.gd and the Player scene to understand the current movement, gravity, jump, and floor-detection logic, and check Project Settings for the jump input action. Confirm whether the project already has a "jump" action mapped and how physics is processed.
2. Define tunable settings at the top of the player script (max air jumps, jump buffer duration of 0.1 s, double-jump velocity) as exported variables so they can be adjusted in the inspector without touching logic.
3. Add state tracking: a counter for air jumps remaining that resets whenever the player is on the floor, and a countdown timer value for the jump buffer.
4. Implement the jump buffer: when jump is pressed, start the 0.1 s countdown; each physics frame decrement it, and if the player is on the floor while the countdown is still positive, perform the jump and clear the buffer.
5. Implement the double jump: if jump is pressed while airborne and air jumps remain, apply the jump velocity, decrement the counter, and clear the buffer so one press never triggers two jumps.
6. Keep existing behaviors intact, including variable jump height on release, and make sure the buffered jump and double jump do not conflict (a buffered press near landing should use the ground jump, not consume the air jump).
7. Test in level_01.tscn by running the scene and checking: early press before landing triggers a jump, a second press mid-air jumps again, a third does nothing, and the counter resets on landing and when walking off ledges. Also verify the enemies and tilemap collisions are unaffected.
8. Optionally add a small visual or audio cue for the double jump, and note the new exported tunables so the developer can adjust feel.

1. Read player.gd and the project's Input Map to learn how movement, gravity, and jump are currently handled, plus any existing coyote-time or floor-check logic. Note which physics callback owns the jump decision.
2. Define the new tunable values as exported variables on the player: buffer window (0.1 s), maximum number of air jumps (1), and the double-jump velocity (defaulting to the same strength as the ground jump, adjustable later).
3. Add a buffer timer that is set to the full window whenever jump is pressed and counts down each physics frame, so a press made just before landing is remembered.
4. Add an air-jump counter that resets whenever the player is on the floor and decrements each time an extra mid-air jump is used.
5. Restructure the jump decision so a jump fires if the buffer is active and the player is grounded, or else if a fresh press occurs in the air with air jumps remaining. Firing a jump consumes the buffer so one press never triggers twice.
6. Keep variable jump height (early release cutting the jump short) working for both jumps, and make sure the double jump overrides any downward velocity so it feels responsive.
7. Check interactions with the enemy scenes (stomp bounces, knockback) and the TileMapLayer edges so those states reset or cancel the air-jump counter and buffer correctly, and add any optional visual or sound cue for the second jump.
8. Playtest in level_01.tscn: verify buffered jumps on landing, a single double jump per airtime, no triple jump, and no double firing, then tune the exported values.

1. Read player.gd and the project's input map to learn how jumping, gravity, floor detection and movement are currently handled, and note any existing jump-related constants or signals.
2. Define tunable settings for the new behavior (maximum number of jumps, buffer duration of 0.1 s) as exported variables on the Player so they can be adjusted in the editor without touching logic.
3. Add jump-count tracking: reset the count whenever the player is on the floor, and allow an extra mid-air jump while the count is below the maximum, so the second jump works after walking off a ledge too.
4. Add a jump buffer timer: when the jump button is pressed while not able to jump, record the press and keep it valid for 0.1 s, counting down each physics frame.
5. Consume the buffer on landing: if a buffered press is still valid the moment the player touches the floor, trigger the jump immediately and clear the buffer.
6. Make sure buffered presses and double jumps don't conflict, for example a buffered press should not also spend the air jump, and each jump should clear the buffer once used.
7. Check that the existing animations, sprite flipping and any enemy stomp or bounce logic still behave correctly with the new jump count, and adjust the jump animation if a second jump needs to restart it.
8. Playtest in level_01.tscn by double jumping, pressing jump just before landing, and jumping off platform edges, then tune the values and confirm nothing regresses with the enemies.

2. Decide where the new tunables live (exported variables on the Player for max air jumps and buffer duration of 0.1 s) so the designer can tweak them in the editor without touching logic.
3. Add jump-buffer logic: when jump is pressed, record a short countdown timer, and each physics frame decrement it so a press made just before landing still counts.
4. Add double-jump logic: track the number of air jumps used, reset it whenever the player is on the floor, and allow an extra jump in mid-air while the count is below the limit.
5. Integrate both in the physics step in the right order: consume the buffered jump when grounded (or when an air jump is available), clear the buffer on use, and apply the same upward velocity so the jumps feel consistent.
6. Check interactions with the rest of the project, such as enemy stomp bounces, any coyote-time or variable-jump-height code, and animation or sprite states, so the new jumps do not break them or double-trigger.

1. Read player.gd and the project's Input Map to learn how movement, gravity, jump velocity, and is_on_floor checks are currently handled, and note any existing coyote-time or state logic.
2. Define tunable exported variables for the buffer window (0.1 s), the maximum number of air jumps (1), and the double-jump strength, so designers can adjust them in the editor without touching logic.
3. Add a jump-buffer timer: when the jump button is pressed, record the press and count it down each physics frame, so a press made up to 0.1 s before landing is remembered.
4. Add an air-jump counter that resets to zero whenever the player is on the floor, and is consumed each time a mid-air jump is performed.
5. Restructure the jump decision into one place: a jump fires if a buffered press exists and the player is grounded (normal jump), or if a fresh press occurs in the air with air jumps remaining (double jump). Clear the buffer whenever a jump fires.
6. Keep variable jump height (early release cuts the jump) working for both jump types, and make sure the double jump overrides downward velocity so it always feels responsive.
7. Hook up feedback hooks, such as an animation or sprite flip and a sound for the double jump, without changing the Sprite2D or CollisionShape2D setup.
8. Playtest in level_01.tscn: verify buffered jumps on landing, double jump from ledges and after falling, no triple jumps, and that enemy contact or respawn resets the counter and buffer correctly. Then tune the values.

4. Consume the buffer on landing: if the buffer is still active the moment the player becomes grounded, trigger the jump automatically and clear the buffer.
5. Add a double jump: track remaining air jumps, reset them to the maximum whenever the player is on the floor, and allow a jump in mid-air while any remain, decrementing each use.
6. Make the two features cooperate: a buffered press should use the ground jump first, an air press with no buffer match should spend an air jump, and a single press must never trigger both. Keep variable-height jump release behavior working for the second jump.

1. Open player.gd and the Player scene to understand the current movement logic: how gravity, ground detection, jump velocity, and input are handled, and which input action is used for jump.
2. Define tunable exported settings on the Player for the maximum number of air jumps (default one), the jump buffer window (0.1 s), and the double-jump strength, so they can be adjusted in the editor without touching logic.
3. Add state tracking for the remaining air jumps and a jump-buffer timer, and reset the air jumps whenever the player is on the floor.
4. Implement the jump buffer: when jump is pressed, record the press for 0.1 s and count it down each physics frame, so a press made just before landing is remembered.
5. Rework the jump handling so a ground jump consumes the buffered press when the player is on the floor, and a press while airborne with air jumps remaining performs the double jump and uses up one air jump.
6. Make sure the interactions are consistent: clear the buffer once a jump fires, keep variable jump height (early release) working for both jumps, and ensure walking off a ledge still allows exactly one extra jump.
7. Check the enemy interactions and level geometry, such as stomping enemies or bounce pads, to confirm they reset or grant air jumps sensibly and that nothing else writes to the vertical velocity in a conflicting way.
8. Playtest in level_01.tscn, verifying a double jump works, a jump pressed up to 0.1 s before landing triggers on touchdown, and no triple jumps or double-fire jumps occur, then tune the values by feel.
